terms.definition: A list of requirements that a type promises to follow, without saying how the work is done.
terms.example: Let's write a protocol for the data service, so we can swap in a fake one in tests.

terms.definition: When a type promises to follow a protocol and provides everything that the protocol asks for.
terms.example: Adding Protocol Conformance to Codable lets us save the model as JSON.

terms.definition: A way to add new features to an existing type, even one you did not write yourself.
terms.example: I wrote an extension on Int to add a squared property, and now we use it everywhere.

facebook.caption:
Hi everyone! Today's iOS Daily English is about protocols and extensions in Swift.

Today's 3 terms:
Protocol - a list of requirements that a type promises to follow.
Protocol Conformance - when a type follows a protocol and provides everything it asks for.
Extension - a way to add new features to an existing type, even one you did not write.

Every example sentence is read twice, normal speed and then slow, so you can say it out loud with us.

There is a short quiz at the end. Drop your answers in the comments, then watch again to check!

dialogue.title: Writing tests: we need a fake data service

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my unit test for the home screen calls the real server. That is slow and flaky.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, a test should not need the network. We need a fake service.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do we swap the real service for a fake one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We write a protocol first. It lists what the service must do, like load users.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the protocol says what, but not how.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The home screen only knows the protocol, not the real class.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the real service and the fake service both have to follow it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is Protocol Conformance. You write a colon and the protocol name after the type.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And if I forget a method, the compiler tells me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Protocol conformance means you provide everything the protocol asks for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote the fake service. But my User model also needs Equatable, and the type is getting long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you add that Protocol Conformance inside the main type?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, all in one block. It feels messy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an extension. You can put the conformance in a separate extension below the type.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh nice. An extension adds features to an existing type.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Even to types you did not write, like Int. I added a squared property last week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. Now my test runs in a few milliseconds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A protocol, a Protocol Conformance, and an extension. Clean and testable.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do we fake the data service?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Write a protocol, and swap in a fake one.
